name: countdown-analytics
description: Countdown to 2030 Shiny apps (RMNCAH, Vaxx, Pooled) and the Countdown AI: grounded answers from the dataset, the methodology docs and what is on screen.

languageModelTools.name: countdown_context
languageModelTools.userDescription: Where you are in a Countdown app: page, what is in view, filters, dataset.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns what the user is looking at in a Countdown app (RMNCAH, Vaxx, Pooled): the tab and dataset (path, country, revision), the dataset's current SELECTIONS (country; the denominator and maternal denominator with their labels; the survey year, source and coverage; the population the growth denominators use; the national rates; the data years and excluded years; the admin levels; the adjustment k-factors; the reporting threshold) -- answer questions about these from here, with no further calls -- the page (id, title, section) with the ESTABLISHED COUNTDOWN METHODOLOGY for that page (full docs sections with URLs, to ground and cite answers), the cards IN VIEW (with the active tab, the component showing, its report kind and options, what that kind shows, the CacheConnection members behind it and its docs), the cards elsewhere on the page, the filters, and other open Countdown tabs. Use it for 'what is this page about', 'what can you see' and 'what does this chart mean' before answering, and to learn which chart 'this' is (if several are in view and the user says 'this chart', ask which). The Shiny App chat context has a shorter version of the same state.

tabId.description: A Countdown app tab id (from countdown_context). Default: the active Countdown tab.

includeMethodology.description: Send the methodology in full even if it was sent for this page recently (e.g. in a new conversation). Default: sent in full once, then only its links.

languageModelTools.name: countdown_component
languageModelTools.userDescription: The data behind a chart or table on screen, with the methodology that explains it.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns the data behind a chart or table in a Countdown app (exactly what its data download writes), together with what it is (its report kind and options, what that kind shows, the CacheConnection members behind it) and the ESTABLISHED COUNTDOWN METHODOLOGY for that chart and its page (full docs sections with URLs), plus the source URLs to cite. Use it -- not screenshots, read_page or shinyApp getComponentData -- whenever the user asks about, interprets or questions a chart or table they are looking at ('tell me about these results', 'what is wrong with my selection', 'does subnational show the same'). Without componentId it takes the one chart in view; if several are in view it fails with their names so you can ask which. Base the answer on the methodology returned and list its URLs under Sources. Prefer it to the generic shinyApp getComponentData: it adds the methodology, the column meanings and the sources.

componentId.description: The component (chart or table) id from countdown_context. Omit for the one chart in view.

maxRows.description: Rows to return (default 40, at most 2000). Ask for more only when the answer needs them.

tabId.description: The Countdown tab (default: the active one).

includeMethodology.description: Send the methodology in full even if it was sent for this page recently (e.g. in a new conversation). Default: sent in full once, then only its links.

languageModelTools.name: countdown_cache
languageModelTools.userDescription: Get data from the open Countdown dataset (CacheConnection).
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Gets data from the Countdown dataset open in a tab by calling ONE member of its CacheConnection, the single source of truth for Countdown numbers (most results are precomputed). Runs in the tab's own read-only R session, on exactly the dataset the app has (reloaded when the app saves). Find the right member with countdown_catalog first; never guess member names or arguments. Arguments not given are filled from the app's current filters where they match (admin_level, region, indicator, denominator), and the reply says which were used. Narrow big results instead of saving and searching them: `where` keeps rows (e.g. {"year": [2021, 2024], "adminlevel_1": "Alibori"}) and `select` keeps columns by name or * pattern (e.g. ["cov_measles1_*"]; the country, level, year and month columns are always kept). Returns the table (capped at maxRows) with provenance (member, arguments, dataset, revision, time): cite it. Use it for any number, on this page or another, national or sub-national, and for drill-downs (decompose_change: which units drive a change between two years). Setters are refused: the AI does not change the dataset.

member.description: A CacheConnection member (method or precomputed binding) from countdown_catalog, e.g. "reporting_rate_district", "get_filtered_coverage", "decompose_change".

args.description: A method's arguments by name, e.g. {"indicator": "anc4", "admin_level": "district"}. Omit for a binding.

maxRows.description: Rows to return (default 200, at most 2000); totalRows says how many there are.

tabId.description: A Countdown app tab id (from countdown_context). Default: the active Countdown tab.

select.description: Columns to keep: names or * patterns, e.g. ["cov_penta3_*", "r_penta3"]. The identifying columns (country, adminlevel_1, district, year, month) are always kept.

where.description: Rows to keep: column = value or list of values, e.g. {"year": [2021], "adminlevel_1": ["Alibori", "Borgou"]}.

languageModelTools.name: countdown_catalog
languageModelTools.userDescription: Find which CacheConnection member or report kind answers a question.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Searches what the Countdown dataset can answer: the read-only members of cd2030.core's CacheConnection (name, group such as 'data quality' or 'coverage', the question it answers, whether it is precomputed, its arguments with allowed values, related report kinds and docs pages), or, with what="reportKinds", the chart and table kinds the apps and reports draw (id, options, members, docs). Use it before countdown_cache to pick the right member and arguments, and before building a report or custom graph. With no query it lists the groups and members.

query.description: Words to match, e.g. "district reporting rate", "coverage anc4", "outliers".

group.description: Only this group (as listed when called with no query).

languageModelTools.name: countdown_docs
languageModelTools.userDescription: Search the Countdown methodology and app documentation.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Searches the Countdown to 2030 methodology and app documentation (https://datasuite.damurka.com): the analysis framework (data quality, adjustment, denominators, coverage, equity, sub-national, mortality, service utilization, health system), indicator definitions, and the RMNCAH, Vaxx and Pooled apps, in English, French or Portuguese. Returns sections with their URLs: cite them. Use it for what a page, chart, indicator or method means and why it matters, and for any general Countdown question, even with no app open. Give url (a page, or page#anchor from a result) to read a whole page or section.

query.description: What to look for, e.g. "how is the denominator selected".

url.description: A docs page or section URL to read in full.

languageModelTools.name: countdown_report
languageModelTools.userDescription: List, build, save, read, change and generate Countdown reports.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Countdown reports (Word, PowerPoint, PDF) are made of blocks: heading, paragraph, note, pagebreak, chart and table (a report kind with options; see listKinds), image. Actions: listPresets (the standard reports); listKinds (chart/table kinds and their options); build (validate a project { name, blocks }); save (validate, then save a NEW report in the dataset, where it opens in the app's Reports page for the user to edit; a custom graph goes in as { type: "chart", kind: "custom_chart", graph: "<saved graph id>" } or with spec; a figure you drew (countdown_graph `figure.path` or countdown_run_r `figures[].path`) goes in as { type: "image", path: "<that path>", caption? } -- saving stores the picture in the dataset, so the report keeps it, but it does not redraw when the data changes: prefer a custom_chart when its data comes from a chartable member); listReports (the saved reports: id, name, kind, lang, blocks); readReport (reportId: its blocks in order -- ids, the text of headings/paragraphs/notes, and for each chart and table its kind, settings, options and a short table of the data it shows -- and its language); updateBlocks (reportId + changes, applied in order, checked as a whole, everything else untouched: { blockId, text } writes or rewrites a heading/paragraph/note (plain text, **bold**, a line break for a new line); { blockId, type: heading|paragraph|note, level }; { blockId, kind, indicator, admin_level, region, year, variant, options: { chart options, null removes one }, size: full|half|third, title, caption: false, pageBreakBefore }; { afterBlockId (or "@start"), insert: { type: paragraph|heading|note|pagebreak|chart|table, text | kind, ... } }; { blockId, delete: true }; { blockId, moveAfter }). To fill in or change a saved report -- its narrative, one paragraph, a chart's kind or options -- readReport then updateBlocks with only what was asked; never save the whole report again (it would wipe the user's edits). generate (write a file from a standard report (preset) or a saved report (reportId), format docx|pptx|pdf, into the tab's working folder). save, updateBlocks and generate change the dataset or write files: only when the user asks. The user's permission setting may ask them to confirm.

preset.description: For generate: a standard report id from listPresets.

reportId.description: For readReport/updateBlocks/generate: a saved report's id (listReports). For save: only to replace that saved report (the user is asked first).

changes.description: For updateBlocks: the changes, applied in order, each naming a block id from readReport.

maxRows.description: For readReport: rows of each chart's data (default 25, at most 100).

data.description: For readReport: false leaves out the charts' data (faster, for text or layout changes).

tabId.description: A Countdown app tab id (from countdown_context). Default: the active Countdown tab.

languageModelTools.name: countdown_graph
languageModelTools.userDescription: Draw a custom graph from the Countdown dataset, and save it.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Draws a custom graph when no report kind fits, from a declarative custom_chart spec: { title, data: { member, args }, transform: [ ... ], plot: { geom, x, y, colour?, fill?, facet?, position?, labels?, percent?, flip? } }. data.member must be a chartable CacheConnection member (countdown_catalog shows 'chartable'); transforms are filter, select, rename, mutate_ratio, aggregate { by, fun, cols }, pivot_longer, arrange, top_n; geoms are line, col, point, area, tile. It validates the spec and draws a preview image (preview, default true), saved in the dataset's analysis folder; the result's `figure.markdown` is a Markdown image of it -- put it in your answer so the user sees the graph (they can click it to open it, or right-click to save it). With save: true it stores the graph in the dataset, where it redraws when the data changes and can be added to any report; do that only when the user wants to keep it (their permission setting may ask them to confirm). No code is stored.

graphId.description: With save: replace this saved graph (the user is asked first); leave it out to add a new one.

save.description: Save it in the dataset (default false).

tabId.description: A Countdown app tab id (from countdown_context). Default: the active Countdown tab.

languageModelTools.name: countdown_documents
languageModelTools.userDescription: Read or search the documents given for this dataset (its documents folder, or a file attached to the chat).
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Reference documents the user gives for the open dataset -- reports, strategies, survey reports, notes -- to use as context (e.g. for a report's text) and to compare with the dataset's results. They are the files in the dataset's analysis folder `documents/`, plus any file the user attached to the chat (pass its full path as `file`; a file outside the documents folder is confirmed with the user first). Actions: list (the documents, with type, size and whether each is indexed for meaning search); read (a document's text by `range` of units -- PDF pages, PowerPoint slides, Word sections by heading, Excel sheets, text chunks -- e.g. "3-5"; each part is headed by its [marker], and at most about 20,000 characters come back, with `next` giving the rest; a scanned page has no text, so its image is attached -- read it from the image); search (across all documents or one `file`: plain words are ranked by keywords and by meaning -- so a question in English, French or Portuguese finds passages in any of them, and scanned pages are found by their image -- best first, each with file, marker, snippet and how it matched (keyword, meaning or both; meaning-only matches can be loose, so read before citing); a "quoted phrase" or a regex with isRegexp finds exact matches instead). Meaning search uses DataSuite's AI service: the documents' text and scanned page images are sent to it to be embedded (once per file version; not when datasuite.embeddings.enabled is off or the user is signed out -- then search is by keywords alone and says why). Formats: PDF (text layer; scanned pages as images), .docx, .pptx, .xlsx/.xls, .csv, text/Markdown. Documents give context, never the dataset's numbers: every figure you give as the dataset's still comes from countdown_cache / countdown_component; when a document's figure differs, show both and say which is which. Cite a document as "<file>, <marker>" (e.g. "National HMIS report 2023.pdf, p. 14") in the Sources.

file.description: read/search: a document's name from list, or the full path of a file attached to the chat. search without it looks in every document.

range.description: read: which units (pages, slides, sections, sheets), 1-based: "3", "3-5" or "3-". Default: from the start.

query.description: search: words or a question (ranked by keywords and meaning), a "quoted phrase" (exact, case-insensitive) or, with isRegexp, a regular expression.

isRegexp.description: search: query is a regular expression (default false).

maxResults.description: search: most matches to return (default 12 ranked, 30 exact).

tabId.description: A Countdown app tab id (from countdown_context). Default: the active Countdown tab.

languageModelTools.name: countdown_run_r
languageModelTools.displayName: Countdown: Run R on the Dataset
languageModelTools.userDescription: Run R on the open Countdown dataset for analysis no member covers.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Runs R code in the tab's own R session (separate from runR's), where `.cache` is the dataset's CacheConnection, opened read-only: the dataset can't be changed from here (reports and graphs are saved with countdown_report / countdown_graph). dplyr, tidyr and cd2030.core are attached. Objects persist between calls on the same tab until its session restarts (the result says so; `.cache` is reloaded then). Only for analysis no single CacheConnection member covers: look with countdown_catalog first, narrow with countdown_cache where/select, and build on members (e.g. `.cache$reporting_rate_district`, `.cache$get_filtered_coverage("anc4", "district")`) rather than raw data. Read all data from .cache -- never type numbers from earlier results or the screen into the code -- and apply only criteria the methodology states. Label what comes from here as computed, not shown in the app. Output: the last visible value is auto-printed; over ~20,000 characters is cut (head and tail kept) -- print compact tables (head(), summarise, select the columns you need); warnings come under [stderr]; errors come with message and backtrace (`status`, `error`). Plots: print() a ggplot (up to 4 attached per call); each is saved in the dataset's analysis folder and listed in `figures` with a ready `markdown` image -- put the ones you discuss in your answer. Code that runs without error is kept in scripts/ as a re-runnable script (`codeSavedTo`). Stops after timeoutSeconds (default 300); objects made before remain. Code that deletes or writes files, runs system commands or installs packages asks the user first.

code.description: R code; print() what you need.

title.description: A few words saying what the code does (e.g. "District reporting gaps 2023"). Names the kept script and figures.

timeoutSeconds.description: Seconds before the run is interrupted (default 300, max 3600).

tabId.description: A Countdown app tab id (from countdown_context). Default: the active Countdown tab.

languageModelTools.name: countdown_open_dataset
languageModelTools.userDescription: Open a Countdown dataset in its own app tab.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Opens a Countdown dataset (a saved .rds, a data file, or for Pooled a folder of .rds files) in its own app tab, so it gets its own context. Use it when the user names a dataset other than the ones open. Picks RMNCAH or Vaxx from the dataset's indicators unless app is given, and Pooled for a folder. Returns the new tab's id for the other countdown_* tools. Asks the user to confirm.

viewsWelcome.contents:
Sign in with your DataSuite account to see the published Countdown datasets you have access to, download them and open them in the RMNCAH or Vaxx app.
[Sign in to DataSuite](command:countdown.datasets.signIn)

You're signed in to DataSuite, but your account doesn't have access to Countdown data yet. Request access: the administrators for your country decide, and the datasets appear here once you're approved.
[Request Access](command:countdown.datasets.requestAccess)
[Try Again](command:countdown.datasets.refresh)

No published datasets for your countries yet. Datasets appear here once a country's final dataset is published. If you expected some, ask your DataSuite administrator which countries you are assigned to.
[Refresh](command:countdown.datasets.refresh)

countdown.ai.useDraftBriefs.markdownDescription: Let the Countdown AI use the methodology docs' AI briefs that are still drafts (not yet checked against the pages). Off: it uses reviewed briefs only, and the full docs sections for pages without one. For trying out briefs before they are reviewed.

countdown.datasets.folder.markdownDescription: Where the Datasets panel keeps the datasets it opens in the apps (each in `<cycle>/<country> v<version>/`, with the app's saved file and analysis folder next to it). Empty: `Documents/Countdown datasets` in your home folder.

countdown.datasets.apiUrl.markdownDescription: The DataSuite API the Datasets panel lists and downloads published datasets from. Change it only to test against another DataSuite server.
